source: A real attached session (`01a1f574-af12-…`, cwd /private/tmp/unbien-capture) recorded by the web client (`?capture=1` tee, then `__unbienDump("023-live-compaction-pair")`). `raw.jsonl` is that dump — UNSCRUBBED, not committed. `capture.py` builds the two committed inputs. Drive sheet: `capture-steps.md`.
extensionVersion: @geohar/un-bien 0.25.15 (the build installed in this pi). The repo's extension source is at 0.25.11; see vocab.md, 'Which build produced this'.
scrub: capture.py, field-aware — the rules 020/021/022 worked out, unchanged: message content is length-preserving `░` filler at any length (row identity is a hash of MESSAGE content, so a marker there breaks the pair), tool-RESULT prose, base64 `data`, `partialResult` and long `details.*` values become `«length»` markers, and shape (`type`, `role`, `mimeType`, `toolCallId`, ids, timestamps, stopReasons, usage) is never touched. NOTE: `summary` on a live `compaction_end` and on a `compaction` ENTRY are scrubbed by the same rule but land on different fillers — which is exactly why no fold may match those two by summary text (see the finding below).
description: The one compaction nobody had watched AND walked: a human attached the client first, filled context with two 120 KB reads, ran `/compact`, then sent one short line so the client would re-walk. The live plane holds the `compaction_end` frame; the trailing walk (72 entries, leaf beacon `83c6e976`) carries the `compaction` ENTRY that IS that compaction, on the active path, along with the session's two earlier compaction entries (`d80b313f` 85 963 tokens, `4156e442` 127 248).
pairing: Same golden in both runners; cold rows contained in the watched rows with identical fields.
trims: One reduction: WALK COLLAPSE, 766 walk runs down to the first and the final (764 dropped — the 6-second re-walk timer is loud once a session is long). Deltas NOT trimmed: 3 turns, 2548 frames, 1.9 MB total.
note: The finding, and it is a nasty one: NO FIELD identifies a compaction. The live `compaction_end` for this `/compact` reported `tokensBefore` 127 248, while the entry that IS that compaction (`8663f793`) recorded 127 749 — the two forms disagree about the count of the same event. And the PREVIOUS compaction's entry (`4156e442`) recorded 127 248 with a **byte-identical summary** (1840 chars, pi regenerated the same text). So a fold that links a live marker to its entry by token count anchors it to the WRONG compaction, and one that links by summary text is ambiguous by construction — the on-screen symptom was four 'Context compacted' rows for three compactions. Both folds now anchor by CAUSALITY instead: compactions are strictly sequential in the log and a walk births entries in log order, so an entry-born compaction anchors the OLDEST live marker not yet anchored, takes the ENTRY's caption (the log's count is what a cold arrival shows), and keeps the row's position. Rule in vocab.md ('One compaction, one row'); pinned by this scenario in both runners and by `web-client/test/compaction-durability.test.ts` and the reference's `SessionStateTests`. The raw dump is NOT retained — 368 MB of unscrubbed wire data, mostly the 766 walk runs the 6-second timer produces. The committed inputs are 1.9 MB and 0.5 MB. Rebuild by following `capture-steps.md`.
